<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A prior conversation referenced a WhatsApp-style PiP pattern from gemini.pdf.

The implementation will be strictly scoped to a single toggle button. It will switch between a split view and a PiP layout where the transformed output is the main video and the camera input appears in a small floating window. Existing camera, microphone, live session, and OBS functionality will remain fully preserved without duplicating streams. The design will stay responsive and avoid any drag-to-snap, double-tap swap, or system PiP interactions.

The toggle will use a CSS class switch on the video container. A header ActionIcon will handle the click and swap between side-by-side and PiP layouts.

The CSS will use a grid layout for the PiP view. The transformed output will fill the container as the main video. The camera input will be absolutely positioned in a small floating window at the bottom-right corner. This preserves the existing DOM order while making the camera appear as a small overlay on top of the main video.

Absolute positioning keeps both video elements and their refs intact during the PiP transition. Placeholders will remain visible in the floating camera window when disconnected. Media queries will scale the pip window down on smaller screens. The toggle button will sit next to the session metadata in the Live preview header.
</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_
